subject: alternative method of incorporating model selection uncertainty

messages.author: caaac2dc0aae28b8
messages.subject: alternative method of incorporating model selection uncertainty
parts:
I would like to get some input on the pros and cons of an alternative met=
hod=20
of incorporating model selection uncertainty into estimates of variance u=
sing=20
bootstrapping in a multiple covariate distance sampling analysis.=20=20

Currently, model averaging is incorporated during the bootstrap option of=
=20
variance estimation. It works by fitting a set of up to 5 detection func=
tions=20
to the bootstrap sample data at each iteration, and the top model being=20=

selected and used for the abundance estimation for that iteration. Model=
=20
selection uncertainty is thereby included in the width of the ensuing=20
confidence intervals calculated from the bootstrap estimates.

My alternative method differs by using a single set of best models, selec=
ted=20
from the original data, to compute a model-average estimate at each=20
iteration. In other words, I first use the original data to select a set=
of best=20
models to use for estimation. Then, at each iteration of the bootstrap I=
=20
compute the model average estimate of abundance based on this set of=20
models and associated parameter estimates. The model average estimate is=
=20
the average of estimates weighted by model weight. The bootstrap=20
abundance estimate and 95% confidence limits are then calculated as usual=
.

An analyst might prefer this method for 2 reasons: 1) For some data (e.g.=
=20
sparse data) there will likely be convergence problems that will go undet=
ected=20
in some (perhaps many) iterations during the automated model selection=20=

occurring in each bootstrap iteration. 2) It is computationally challeng=
ing to=20
have to re-fit a set of detection functions at each iteration, especially=
when=20
covariates differ across models in multiple covariate distance sampling.

The basic question is: "does my proposed method adequately incorporate=20=

model selection uncertainty, given the constraints I mention?"
